title: Response Economy Labbook — Microcredits & Graceful Degradation
content:
Notes to self — messy brain dump / proto-PRD for a small experiment that could reduce token spend while preserving perceived quality for chat/assistant products. Goal is to sketch a feature that lives between full quantization/architecture changes and product-side heuristics: an inference-level micro-economy that budgets tokens per session and gracefully degrades fidelity with clear UX signals.

Context and motivation:
- We keep getting requests from product teams to reduce per-session token costs without shredding UX. Dedicated + Hosted customers care about predictability: predictable tail latency and cost.
- Existing levers: batching, KV caching, quant profiles, model switching. But these are coarse-grained and either offline or global.
- Idea: add a runtime-aware "microcredit" layer that:
  1) allocates a small token budget per user session based on tier/activity signals,
  2) intercepts outgoing token generation requests and applies lightweight fidelity controls (response length cap, sampling temperature adjustment, fallback to compressed recaps or retrieval snippets),
  3) surfaces signals to client (headers/metadata) so UX can show a subtle affordance ("economy mode") and product can decide to purchase or top-up credits.

Key properties (early thinking):
- Runtime-first: implemented in serving/runtime layer (or sidecar) so it can leverage real-time metrics (latency, per-session token burn, model selection).
- Pluggable policies: per-tenant, per-route, and per-session policies (e.g., free-tier sessions get 800 microcredits/day, enterprise gets higher baseline).
- Non-blocking degraded responses: when budget low, runtime chooses cheaper op (short recap + ask to continue, compressed excerpt, or use a smaller model) instead of failing.
- Telemetry-first: must emit token-level and action-level telemetry (why we trimmed, what fallback chosen, latency impact).

Feature sketch / components:
1) Microcredit allocator
   - Inputs: tenant tier, route, recent token consumption, session signals (active user, retention score), on-call product overrides.
   - Output: int credits remaining, per-request allowance.
2) Fidelity controller (runtime hook)
   - Intercepts generate calls and returns one of: FULL, TRIM, PEEK, SMALL_MODEL.
   - Rules: if predicted response tokens > allowance, choose TRIM or PEEK. TRIM: prefer compressive rewrite; PEEK: return a short pointer + call-to-action. SMALL_MODEL: route to compatible cheaper variant.
3) UX signal layer (response metadata)
   - Add headers: X-RW-Microcredits-Remaining, X-RW-Fidelity-Decision, X-RW-Fallback-Reason. Product teams can surface small banners or rate-limit behavior.
4) Admin / policy UI (initially under Console Optimize)
   - Policy templates (aggressive, balanced, generous), per-tenant tuning, manual top-up.

Concrete user stories (draft):
- As a product manager on free tier, I want my users to be able to have 3 low-cost sessions per day so we don’t blow trial credits, while still providing helpful answers. Acceptance: free sessions see "economy mode" indicator and answers are shorter but not silent fail.
- As an enterprise admin, I want to set a high baseline and a fallback policy that uses a regionally cheaper model instead of trimming when latency is degraded. Acceptance: when trace shows heavy load, traffic flows to smaller-model variant and SLA maintained.
- As an SRE, I want to observe fidelity-change events in tracing so we can correlate with spikes in latency and token burn. Acceptance: traces show X-RW-Fidelity-Decision and fallback reason for >=95% of degraded responses.

Telemetry & metrics (important):
- Primary metrics: tokens-per-session, percent responses served by fallback, average latency by decision type, customer-visible satisfaction (NPS/qual surveys where available).
- Safety metrics: instances of truncated answers that led to follow-up queries (proxy for degraded UX).
- Cost math: estimate delta tokens saved per fallback * token unit cost => projected savings for hosted pool.

Experiment matrix (small incremental rollout):
- Phase 0: offline simulation (use logs to simulate microcredit decisions against historical traffic — estimate savings and regression on answer length).
- Phase 1: internal beta (redwood employees + trusted customer) — soft signal to client, not enforce hard trimming (log-only + recommended decisions).
- Phase 2: opt-in product flag for select customers (10% of free-tier, 5% of paid experiments). Track satisfaction.
- Phase 3: gradual default enablement with policy templates.

Open questions / risks (notes):
- UX risk: users may feel cheated if answer is truncated without clear signal. Need careful wording and CTA ("expand / continue to full answer – uses tokens").
- Model compatibility: smaller cheaper variants must be compatible with current prompt and function-calling expectations. Model switcher needs to handle tool-calls gracefully.
- Billing complexity: microcredits map to token accounting — need clear mapping and billing adjustments to avoid disputes.
- Operational complexity: additional routing and fidelity decision logic may add latency. Must be microsecond-light and cacheable.

Implementation notes (runtime-centric):
- Implement fidelity controller as a short-circuiting middleware in the serving-runtime (same process or sidecar). Keep logic deterministic and small.
- Predictor: a cheap heuristic to estimate output tokens (based on prompt length + historical length, or use a tiny per-route ML model offline).
- Fallback repertoire: compressive rewrite (LLM prompt that asks for short summary), length cap + high-temp sampling, small-model routing, or precompute recap with retrieval. Order of preference configurable per tenant.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Runtime exposes hook and metadata headers.
- Admin can set 3 policy templates and apply to a tenant.
- Telemetry emits fidelity decisions with trace links.
- Simulated rollout shows >=20% token savings on targeted routes with <8% rise in follow-up queries.

Next steps / TODO (short):
- Run offline simulation on last 30 days of chat traffic for two top product routes (assistant-chat, helpdesk-reply). Owner: me (Daniela). Target: 2 working days.
- Draft a short Confluence page + slide for product review (link to this doc). Collaborators: Mika (experiment design), Noah (telemetry + SLI).
- Quick spike: implement a log-only fidelity controller in local runtime devkit to prove headers and decision types. Timebox: 3 days.

Links / refs:
- Simulate query: GH-PR providing the log replay tool (GH-PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/219)
- Policy idea thread: Slack: #product-econ (see thread ts 2026-02-10)

Rough schedule (very rough):
Week 0: simulation + cost estimate
Week 1: internal beta + telemetry hooks
Week 2-4: opt-in customer experiments, iterate wording and policies

Random parking-lot ideas:
- Charge a tiny fee to users to "boost" their microcredits in-session (microtransactions) — controversial but worth noticing for paid products.
- Let client-side heuristics request an "economy hint" to prefer retrieval-based answers over generation when credits low.
- A/B test UX wording: "economy mode" vs "concise mode" vs no-label.

End of messy notes. Will refine after simulation results.

---
Personal note: keep this small and measurable. Avoid friction with billing/policy ownership — coordinate early with finance & billing SME.
